land.text: Ghazni, Kabul and the south-east of Afghanistan of Cliopatria's 1206 shape

successors.note: 'Yildiz established himself as the king of Ghazni in 1206' (Muhammad of Ghor page); he held it, nominally under Ghurid authority, until the Khwarazmians defeated him there in 1215. Needs a dossier (not written by this batch).

capitals.name: Firozkoh (Jam, Ghor)
capitals.note: Ghiyath al-Din 'governed from Fīrōzkōh' while Muhammad's capital 'was in Ghazni'; the site of Firozkoh is the Minaret of Jam region, the coordinates are approximate. Ghiyath kept Firozkoh and Herat as his seats to 1203.

capitals.name: Ghazni
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Firozkoh, Herat, Ghazni (1170s-1215)'; Muhammad of Ghor was crowned at Ghazni in 1173 and 'expanded the Ghurid domains eastwards into the Indian plains from his capital at Ghazni'. Taken by the Khwarazmians in 1215.

rulers.name: Ala al-Din Husayn
rulers.note: Reign 1149-1161 on the coinage table; 'defeated and captured at Nab in the Harirud Valley by Sultan Ahmed Sanjar' in 1152; sacked Ghazni.

rulers.name: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad
rulers.note: Co-ruled in a dyarchy with his brother Muhammad of Ghor from 1173; died at Herat on 13 March 1203.

rulers.name: Muhammad of Ghor (Mu'izz al-Din)
rulers.note: Co-ruler at Ghazni from 1173 ('diarchy 1173-1206' on the infobox); sole ruler from 1203; assassinated 15 March 1206.

rulers.name: Ghiyath al-Din Mahmud
rulers.note: Khwarazmian vassal on the coinage table (1206-1215); authority in India limited.

keyframe_review.note: 1.83 M km2 against 1202's 2.14 M: the Cliopatria shape loses Herat and most of Ghor (the Khwarazmians 'captured Herat and Ghor in 1206') but still holds Ghazni, Kabul and all the Indian conquests, which in 1206 went to others: Delhi, Lahore and Ajmer to Aibak (25 June 1206, 'became the sultan of Delhi, establishing the Mamluk dynasty'), Multan and Uch to Qabacha, Bayana to Tughril, Bihar and Bengal to Bakhtiyar Khalji's successors, and Ghazni to Yildiz ('Yildiz established himself as the king of Ghazni in 1206' after receiving a chatr from Mahmud, Muhammad of Ghor page; 'Tajuddin Elduz became the ruler of Ghazni', Ghurid page). The corrected shape keeps only what the Ghurid sultans, Khwarazmian vassals from 1206 (coinage table), still held: the Ghor province and Bamiyan, to 1215. Reading of the pages, uncertain about the frontier. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Ghazni and Kabul were drawn Ghurid to 1215 although Yildiz had taken Ghazni in 1206; reading (a): Yildiz rules Ghazni for himself, recognising Ghurid authority only nominally (Yildiz page: 'de facto ruler of Ghazni, while ... still recognizing Ghurid authority'). Kabul is named by no page; it goes with Ghazni.]

region.text: the Ghor highlands with Firozkoh and Bamiyan

ledger.note: 1152: the Ghurids of Ghor, vassals of the Seljuks, appear in Cliopatria. The page dates the dynasty to 786 ('Established: 786') and has them rule 'initially ... as vassals of the Ghaznavids and later of the Seljuks'; in 1152 Ala al-Din Husayn 'was defeated and captured at Nab in the Harirud Valley by Sultan Ahmed Sanjar'. 1152 is Cliopatria's first shape, not a page's founding date. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: confidence 1 to 2: the Ala al-Din Husayn page has 'In 1152, he declared independence against his Seljuq overlords, and captured Balkh' and then 'defeated and captured by Ahmad Sanjar' (released after two years for a ransom), as the Ghurid page has the refusal of tribute in 1152; the Seljuk overlordship before 1152 is therefore on a page, the Balkh of 1152 was held only briefly and is not drawn.]

region.text: Sistan, the country of the Nasrid dynasty

ledger.note: 1162: the Nasrid dynasty of Sistan becomes a Ghurid vassal. 'They became vassals of the Seljuks in 1048, Ghurids in 1162, and the Khwarezmians in 1212' (Sistan page, about the Nasrid dynasty, which the Khwarezmians ended in 1225). The region is the Sistan region (the Sistan region lies entirely inside Cliopatria's 1177 Ghurid shape, which holds it from 1177); the Ghurid page says the Ghurids 'took control of the areas of Nimruz and Sistan' without a year. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: Cliopatria holds Sistan from 1177 and no page opened mentioned it.]

region.text: the city of Ghazni, from the Ghuzz Turks

ledger.note: 1173: Muhammad of Ghor takes Ghazni. 'In 1173, Muhammad of Ghor after multiple attempts reconquered the city of Ghazni from the Ghuzz Turks'; the Muhammad of Ghor page gives both 1169 ('conquering Ghazni in 1169') and 'Muhammad's coronation took place in Ghazni in 1173'. The radius around the city is mine.
1173: Muhammad of Ghor is crowned at Ghazni and holds it as his seat; his brother Ghiyath al-Din returns to Firuzkuh. Infobox capitals 'Firozkoh, Herat, Ghazni (1170s-1215)'.

1175: the Ghurids take Herat from the Seljuks. 'In 1175, the Ghurids took control of Herat from the Seljuks' (the Muhammad of Ghor page: 'helped his brother with the annexation of the cities of Herat and Pushang', after defeating a former Seljuk general).
1175: Muhammad takes Multan from the Qarmatians. 'Muhammad defeated the Qarmatian ruler Khafif in 1175 and annexed Multan.'

1176: Uch. 'also took Uch by 1176'; the Muhammad of Ghor page's infobox puts Uch in 1175 ('captured Multan and Uch from the Carmathians within a year') and its body after 1179. Coordinates approximate (Uch is not in the gazetteer).

region.text: Naddula (Nadol) and the foot of Mount Abu, the Chaulukya northern marches

ledger.note: 1178: the Ghurid army marches on Gujarat and is routed at Kasahrada (Mount Abu). 'His army was routed by the Chaulukya (Solanki) king Mularaja II and allied Rajput chiefs' (the page confirms 1178 only through Aibak's later avenging attack 'at the same place'). No ground was taken; the zone is the one the chaulukya-dynasty dossier uses.

region.text: Naddula (Nadol) and the foot of Mount Abu

ledger.note: 1178: the Ghurid retreat from Mount Abu ends the first Gujarat campaign; the next attack on Gujarat is Aibak's of 1197.
1179: Peshawar. 'In 1179, Muhammad conquered Peshawar', from the Ghaznavids 'who possibly held it'; the Ghurid dynasty page says only 'by the turn of next decade'.

region.text: the port city of Debal and the Soomra country

ledger.note: 1182: the Soomras of Sindh submit. 'In 1182, Muhammad followed a southerly arc to the port city of Debal' and subjugated the Soomras there; the page gives no frontier, the region is Sindh. No land changes hands (sa-03's soomra-dynasty dossier makes the same point).

region.text: Lahore and the last Ghaznavid lands in the Punjab

ledger.note: 1186: Lahore falls and the Ghaznavids end. 'ended the Ghaznavids rule in 1186 CE'; Khusrau Malik was captured and later executed c. 1192 at Firuzkuh.

region.text: Tabarhindah (Bathinda) and Tarain (Taraori), the frontier of Haryana and Punjab

ledger.note: 1190: the Ghurid generals take Bathinda and open the war with the Chahamanas. 'captured the fortress of Bathinda' (1190); the Tabarhind garrison then 'held out for thirteen months before capitulating'. Zone as in the chauhan-dynasty dossier.

region.text: Tarain and the frontier of Haryana and Punjab

ledger.note: 1192: the Second Battle of Tarain ends the contest. Prithviraj, who had beaten Muhammad at the First Battle (1191), is routed 'in the return engagement on the same battleground' and executed 'shortly afterwards'.

region.text: the former Chahamana territory around Kuhram and Samana

ledger.note: 1192: Haryana passes to the Ghurids under Aibak. 'Muhammad Ghori gave Aibak the former Chahamana territory, based at Kuhram' (governor of Kuhram and Samana); Meerut and Baran taken in 1192. The chauhan-dynasty dossier records Delhi and Haryana together in 1192; here Delhi follows below (vassal 1192, direct 1193).

1192: Delhi under a Tomara vassal. Aibak 'took control in 1192 and kept the Tomara ruler as a vassal'. [Reviewer sa-04-a: counterpart changed from 'tomara-dynasty', whose dossier ends in 1152 (succeeded by chauhan-dynasty); the Aibak page has 'the local Tomara ruler' kept 'as a vassal' in 1192 and deposed in 1193]

region.text: Ajmer and the Chahamana kingdom in Rajasthan

ledger.note: 1192: Ajmer submits. Govindaraja IV 'submitted to the Ghurids the region of Ajmer, which became a vassal state' after Second Tarain.

1193: Delhi annexed. 'In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi' (the Ghurid page: 'In 1193, Delhi was conquered by ... Qutbu l-Din Aibak'). [Reviewer sa-04-a: counterpart changed from 'tomara-dynasty', whose dossier ends in 1152 (succeeded by chauhan-dynasty); the Aibak page has 'the local Tomara ruler' kept 'as a vassal' in 1192 and deposed in 1193]

1193: the Ghurids rule Delhi directly. [Reviewer sa-04-a: counterpart changed from 'tomara-dynasty', whose dossier ends in 1152 (succeeded by chauhan-dynasty); the Aibak page has 'the local Tomara ruler' kept 'as a vassal' in 1192 and deposed in 1193]
1194: Muhammad crosses the Yamuna against the Gahadavalas. 'in 1194, he crossed the Jamuna River with an army of 50,000 horsemen'; Varanasi was looted, Sarnath sacked.
1194: the Battle of Chandawar. 'Jayachandra was killed in the battle.'
1194: Koil (Aligarh). Aibak crossed the Yamuna and captured Koil 'from the Dor Rajputs' in 1194.

1194: Ajmer under a Muslim governor. 'Aibak subsequently placed Ajmer under a Muslim governor' (after Chandawar, 1194); the chauhan-dynasty dossier ends the Chahamana state with Hariraja's defeat in 1194. The page gives no year for the replacement.

c. 1196: Bayana and Thankar. 'Muhammad returned to the Indian frontier again around 1196'; Thankar's ruler Kumarpal was defeated and Bahauddin Tughril took control of Bayana (Gwalior fell to Tughril later, undated). Coordinates approximate (Bayana is not in the gazetteer).

1197: Aibak sacks Anhilwara. 'In 1197, Qutb ud-Din Aibak invaded' Gujarat, defeated Bhima II at Sirohi and 'sacked his capital Anhilwara'; Bhima fled the city, 'plundered by the invaders'. Aibak's page: Ghurid control there did not last.

ledger.counterpart: Balkh vassal (the page does not name the holder)
ledger.note: 1198: Muhammad of Ghor seizes Balkh. 'In 1198, Muhammad of Ghor, one of the Ghurid rulers, seized Balkh from the vassal of the Qara Khitai'; 'The Ghurids kept Balkh and the Amu Darya was agreed upon as the border between the two realms'. The counterpart string is the one kara-khitans ledger 1198 (vassal_end) uses. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Balkh was missing from the ledger; the Muhammad of Ghor page has Ghiyath al-Din capturing 'Balkh and territories adjoining Herat' without a year.]

1198: Kannauj. 'The Gahadavala capital Kanauj was annexed in 1198' (Aibak's page: Kannauj captured in 1198-1199). The gahadavala-dynasty dossier hands its realm to the Ghurids at the 1194 defeat; Cliopatria's Ghurid shape covers it from 1202.
1197-1198: Budaun. Aibak 'conquered' Budaun ('Budaun (1197-98)'); the page does not name the ruler.

region.text: Nishapur, Merv and Tus and the Khorasan oasis cities

ledger.note: 1200: Muhammad and Ghiyath al-Din take Khorasan. 'The Ghurids then took control of all Khorasan following the death of ... Tekish in 1200'; Muhammad and Ghiyath al-Din 'invaded and captured the oasis cities of Nishapur, Merv and Tus'. [Reviewer sa-04-a: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Khurasan, Nishapur, Merv and Tus, not the whole of Turkmenistan in the region] [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: region: {country: Turkmenistan} replaced by {admin1: Mary} (Merv); the page names only Khurasan, Nishapur, Merv and Tus.]

1200: Bihar. The Muhammad of Ghor page says only that his lieutenants, 'notably Bakhtiyar Khalji', extended influence east, with northern Bihar mentioned, and gives no date; 1200 is the year the sena-dynasty dossier (sa-03) records the loss of Bihar, and Cliopatria's 1202 shape reaches it. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: source changed from the Muhammad of Ghor page, confidence 1 to 2: the Bakhtiyar Khalji page has 'He subjugated much of Bihar in 1200' (the region, all of Bihar, is my reading of 'much of').]

1201: Anhilwara back in Chaulukya hands. The Muhammad of Ghor page says nothing of the end of the occupation (Aibak's page: Ghurid control there 'did not last'); 1201 is the year the chaulukya-dynasty dossier (sa-03) records. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: source changed to the Chaulukya page, confidence 1 to 2: 'the capital was back under the Chaulukya rule by 1201 CE' after Bhima's generals 'forced the Ghurids to retreat' (a bound; the same page dates Aibak's invasion of Anahilapataka to 4 February 1197).]

region.text: Nishapur, Merv and Tus and the Khorasan oasis cities

ledger.note: 1201: Khorasan lost again. Alauddin Shah 'recaptured his lost territories' 'by 1201'; Muhammad 'later retook Tus and Herat' (undated). [Reviewer sa-04-a: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Khurasan, Nishapur, Merv and Tus, not the whole of Turkmenistan in the region] [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: region: {country: Turkmenistan} replaced by {admin1: Mary} (Merv); the page names only Khurasan, Nishapur, Merv and Tus.]

region.text: Kalinjar, the hill fort, with Mahoba and Khajuraho

ledger.note: 1203: Kalinjar. The siege was in 1202 and 'Their former strongholds of Kalinjar, Mahoba, and Khajuraho came under Ghurid control' (1202-1203, no exact date; the chandela-kingdom dossier gives 27 April 1203).

1204: the defeat at Andkhud. Muhammad 'decisively defeated in the Battle of Andkhud in 1204' by the Qara Khitai and Kara-Khanid forces and paid a ransom; 'Most of Khorasan was lost except Herat and Balkh'. After he besieged Gurganj the Qara Khitai intervened.

region.text: Bengal, Lakhnauti (the Sena capital) and the Rarh and Varendra country

ledger.note: 1205: Lakhnauti. Around 1203 Bakhtiyar Khalji 'swept down the lower Gangetic Plain and into Bengal' and 'established Islamic government at Lakhnauti in 1205'; Aibak's page has Khalji conquer 'a part of the Bengal region' and honoured by Aibak in March 1203. The sena-dynasty dossier dates the Sena loss 1204. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: region: all of Bangladesh replaced by the mamluk-dynasty region (West Bengal, Rajshahi, Rangpur); the page names only Lakhnauti, and sena-dynasty keeps east Bengal until 1230.]

1205: Kalinjar leaves Ghurid hands. The pages opened give no end; 1205 is the year the chandela-kingdom dossier (sa-03) records. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: the Chandela dynasty page was opened and does not have the 1205 inscription ('Kalanjaradhipati') or any date for Kalinjar after Aibak's invasion 'around 1202-1203'; confidence stays 1.]

1206: the Khwarazmians take Herat and Ghor. 'The Khwarezmians under Ala al-Din Muhammad captured Herat and Ghor in 1206, and finally Ghazni in 1215'; the Ghurid page's coinage table has the rulers of 1206-1215 as Khwarazmian vassals. [Reviewer sa-04-a: source changed from Khwarazmian_Empire, which does not have this sentence; the Ghurid dynasty page does ('captured Herat and Ghor in 1206, and finally Ghazni in 1215')] [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the region stays Herat; the Ghor province and Bamiyan remain with the Ghurid sultans as Khwarazmian vassals (vassal_start below), as in the coinage table.]

1206: Qabacha holds Multan and Uch. 'Uch was held by Qabacha after Aitam's death (1204)' and the Muhammad page's infobox lists him at Multan; Qabacha was Iltutmish's rival until 1228. The page gives no frontier, the radius around Multan is mine.

region.text: Bihar and Bengal, Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquests

ledger.note: 1206: Bakhtiyar Khalji's Bihar and Bengal. He 'was not Aibak's subordinate when he died in 1206' (Aibak page); the Muhammad page lists Bengal under Bakhtiyar Khalji among the lands divided after the assassination. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: region: all of Bangladesh replaced by Rajshahi and Rangpur, as in mamluk-dynasty.]
1206: Tughril at Bayana. After Muhammad's death 'Tughril styled himself sultan at Bayana' (the page's Bayana is Bahauddin Tughril's, who 'reduced Gwalior' undated). Coordinates approximate.
1206: the Soomra vassalage lapses with Muhammad of Ghor's death. The pages give no end date for the 1182 submission; Qabacha held Multan and Uch after 1206 and Sindh is not named again.

1206 or soon after: Balkh passes to Khwarazm. After Muhammad's death Ghiyath asked Muhammad II of Khwarazm for help, 'but Muhammad instead invaded Ghiyath's domains, capturing Balkh and Termez' (Yildiz page, no year); Muhammad's viceroy still held Balkh in July 1205 (Qara Khitai page: 'In the summer of 1205, the Ghurid viceroy in Balkh seized Tirmidh') and the Muhammad of Ghor page has Herat and Balkh Ghurid after Andkhud (1204). 1206 is a bridge between those, the pages give no year. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Balkh had no loss event.]

region.text: Ghazni, Kabul and the south-east of Afghanistan that Cliopatria's 1206 shape holds (Zabul, Paktika, Kandahar, Helmand, Nimruz): the Afghan part of that shape outside the Ghor and Bamyan provinces

ledger.note: 1206: Yildiz takes Ghazni. 'Yildiz established himself as the king of Ghazni in 1206', after receiving a chatr from Mahmud (Muhammad of Ghor page); 'Tajuddin Elduz became the ruler of Ghazni' (Ghurid page); he 'seized the city from the Bamiyan Ghurids' and was 'de facto ruler of Ghazni, while ... still recognizing Ghurid authority' (Yildiz page, no year). Reading (a): he rules Ghazni for himself, the Ghurid tie being nominal. Kabul is named by no page and goes with Ghazni. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Ghazni was kept Ghurid to 1215 in the keyframes while this dossier also asked for a Yildiz dossier; it is now Yildiz's from 1206, and Khwarazm takes it from Yildiz in 1215.]

region.text: the Ghor province (Firozkoh) and Bamiyan, the Ghurid sultans' remnant

ledger.note: 1206 (after the assassination of 15 March): the Ghurid sultans become Khwarazmian vassals. The coinage table heads the rulers of 1206-1215 'As vassals of the Khwarazmian Empire' ('Green shaded row signifies Ghurid vassalage under the Khwarazmian dynasty'); the Khwarazm page has the Khwarazmians 'sweeping aside the Ghurids in 1215, whom they vassalized after the assassination of Muhammad Ghuri'. The page names no frontier: Ghor and Bamiyan are my reading of what the sultans still held, hence confidence 2 (the reviewer proposed 3). [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the Ghurid side of the vassalage was missing; the khwarezmid-empire dossier carries the overlord's side.]

region.text: Lahore, Delhi, the Doab and Ajmer, Aibak's share of Muhammad's Indian conquests

ledger.note: 1206: Aibak founds the Delhi Mamluk dynasty. Muhammad of Ghor was 'assassinated near the Indus on March 15, 1206' (at Dhamiak); Aibak 'informally ascended the throne on 25 June 1206' at Lahore and, the Muhammad page says, 'declared independence in 1208'; the Mamluk page: he 'became the sultan of Delhi, establishing the Mamluk dynasty'. The land is Cliopatria's 1210 Mamluk shape (Lahore, Delhi, the Doab) with Ajmer; Ghiyath al-Din Mahmud's authority in India was limited.

region.text: Sistan, the country of the Nasrid dynasty

ledger.note: 1212: the Nasrids of Sistan are Khwarazmian vassals (the same sentence). The Ghurid sultans were themselves Khwarazmian vassals from 1206 (ledger), so the Ghurid overlordship of Sistan ends no later than 1212; Cliopatria's 1206-1209 shape no longer holds Sistan.

region.text: the Ghor province (Firozkoh) and Bamiyan, the Ghurid sultans' remnant

ledger.note: 1215: Muhammad II ends the Ghurid vassalage. 'Shah Muhammad II uprooted the Ghurids in 1215'; the Yildiz page has him conquer Firuzkuh 'one year later' than 1214. The vassal land passes to Khwarazm outright (dissolve). [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: vassal_end for the vassal_start of 1206.]

region.text: the Ghor province (Firozkoh) and Bamiyan, the Ghurid remnant

ledger.note: 1215: Khwarazm ends the Ghurid dynasty. 'Shah Muhammad II uprooted the Ghurids in 1215'; 'The Khwarezmians under Ala al-Din Muhammad captured Herat and Ghor in 1206, and finally Ghazni in 1215'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1215'. The Yildiz page has Muhammad II conquer Firuzkuh after 1214 and then defeat Yildiz at Ghazni, so the Ghazni of 1215 is taken from Yildiz, not from the Ghurid sultans. Yildiz, driven out of Ghazni, was executed in 1216 (Muhammad of Ghor page). [Reviewer sa-04-a: source changed from Khwarazmian_Empire, which does not have this sentence; the Ghurid dynasty page does ('captured Herat and Ghor in 1206, and finally Ghazni in 1215')] [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: region narrowed from Ghazni and the remnant to Ghor and Bamiyan, because Ghazni has been Yildiz's since 1206.]

wars.name: Ghurid-Ghaznavid war and conquest of the Punjab
wars.outcome: Ghazni 1173, Peshawar 1179, the last Ghaznavid strongholds attacked in 1181 under Khusrau Malik, Lahore taken in 1186, which 'ended the Ghaznavids rule'.
wars.note: The Ghurid page says the Peshawar-Sindh conquests came 'by the turn of next decade'; the Muhammad of Ghor page gives the individual years used here.

wars.name: Ghurid invasion of Gujarat (Battle of Kasahrada)
wars.outcome: Ghurid army routed by Mularaja II and Rajput allies at Kasahrada; no ground taken.

wars.name: First and Second Battles of Tarain
wars.outcome: Bathinda taken 1190; Muhammad wounded in the First Battle of Tarain (1191); Prithviraj routed in 1192 and executed; Delhi and Ajmer pass to the Ghurids (Delhi directly 1193, Ajmer as a vassal).

wars.name: Battle of Chandawar
wars.outcome: Jayachandra killed; Varanasi looted and Sarnath sacked; Kannauj annexed in 1198.

wars.name: Aibak's Gujarat campaign
wars.outcome: Aibak defeats Bhima II at Sirohi and sacks Anhilwara; control did not last.

wars.name: Siege of Kalinjar
wars.outcome: Kalinjar, Mahoba and Khajuraho 'came under Ghurid control'.

wars.name: Ghurid-Khwarazmian war for Khorasan

zones.text: Nishapur, Merv and Tus and the Khorasan oasis cities

wars.outcome: Nishapur, Merv and Tus taken 1200 and recovered by Khwarazm by 1201; Muhammad defeated at Andkhud in 1204 by the Qara Khitai and Khwarazmians and loses most of Khorasan; Herat and Balkh stay Ghurid until 1206.
wars.note: The Khwarazmian Empire page is silent on all of this.

wars.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of Bihar and Bengal
wars.outcome: Bihar and the lower Ganges plain overrun; 'Islamic government' at Lakhnauti in 1205.
wars.note: Muhammad of Ghor page: no dates for Bihar and Bengal. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: zone widened from Bihar and West Bengal to include Rajshahi and Rangpur, the same Lakhnauti country as ledger 1205 and mamluk-dynasty.]

wars.name: Khwarazmian conquest of Ghur and Ghazni
wars.outcome: Herat and Ghor 1206, Ghazni 1215; the Ghurid rulers of 1206-1215 are Khwarazmian vassals.

certainty.note: Every Ghurid frontier is approximate: the pages name cities and campaigns, not boundaries. The Khorasan frontier (1200-1204) and the vassal Rajput states are the softest.

notes:
Cliopatria's Ghurid row (1152-1209) is read against five pages. START: the infobox gives 786 and the dynasty ruled as vassal of the Ghaznavids and Seljuks; 1152 is Cliopatria's first shape (the page has Ala al-Din Husayn defeated at Nab by Sanjar that year), so the found event is confidence 1; a gap-filler should open 'Ala al-Din Husayn' (not opened: page budget) for the independence and the 1150s sack of Ghazni. END: the dossier ends in 1215 (infobox 'Disestablished 1215'; Ghazni falls to Khwarazm); Cliopatria ends 1209, so keyframe ghurid-dynasty_1210 (new) covers 1210-1215, and 1206-1215 is drawn as a Khwarazmian-vassal remnant (Ghazni, Kabul, Ghor, Bamiyan): this is a reading of the coinage table and the Khwarazm page, not a dated frontier. The mirror for the Khwarazm side (vassal_start for Ghur 1206-1215, counterpart ghurid-dynasty) belongs in the khwarezmid-empire dossier. THE INDIAN LANDS: Cliopatria draws Muhammad's whole Indian empire (Punjab, Sindh, Delhi, Rajasthan, Bihar) as Ghurid to 1209 and Mamluk from 1210 with a much smaller shape; on the pages Aibak ascended on 25 June 1206 and the other commanders (Yildiz at Ghazni, Qabacha at Multan and Uch, Tughril at Bayana, Bakhtiyar Khalji in Bihar and Bengal) held their own lands. The mamluk-dynasty dossier carries the 1206-1209 Delhi shape; the other commanders' states need dossiers (Qabacha of Multan, Yildiz of Ghazni, the Khalji dynasty of Bengal). PAGES DISAGREE: Ghazni 1169 vs 1173; Uch 1175/1176/after 1179; Delhi 1192 vs 1193; Sindh/Peshawar 'by the turn of next decade' vs Peshawar 1179 and Debal 1182; Kannauj 1198 (Muhammad page) vs the gahadavala-dynasty dossier's 1194 handover. NOT SETTLED: Balkh (held 1204-1205 per the Muhammad page, not in Cliopatria's shape, no acquisition date); Gwalior (Tughril, undated); Sistan (Cliopatria's shapes hold about 900 cells in Iran from 1177; no page opened mentions it); the Ghurid frontier west of Herat before 1200. Pages opened: 5 of 5; the Khwarazmian page was almost silent on the Ghurids. Gazetteer: 'Uch', 'Bayana', 'Debal' are not places in the gazetteer (coordinates used for Uch and Bayana); 'Nadol', 'Bathinda', 'Anahilapataka' and 'Kalinjar' are real names the gazetteer lacks and are left as names (they resolve to nothing until the gazetteer has them).

Repair pass (sa-04-a, 2026-10-19): vassal_start 1206 / vassal_end 1215 to khwarezmid-empire added (confidence 2, the region is my reading); Balkh added (gain 1198 from the Qara Khitai vassal, loss 1206 to Khwarazm at confidence 1; keyframes ghurid-dynasty_1198, _1200, _1201, _1202); Ghazni and Kabul go to Yildiz from 1206 (reading a of the reviewer, the Ghurid tie nominal), so KF6/KF7 and the 1215 dissolve now hold only Ghor and Bamiyan; new keyframes ghurid-dynasty_1173 and _1175 draw the 1173-1176 gains; Bengal regions narrowed to West Bengal, Rajshahi and Rangpur; Khorasan regions use Mary (Merv) instead of all Turkmenistan.

Thin findings tried (sa-04-a repair): /ledger/0 raised to 2 (Ala al-Din Husayn page); Bihar 1200 raised to 2 (Bakhtiyar Khalji page); Anhilwara end raised to 2 (Chaulukya page); Kalinjar 1205 still unsupported (Chandela dynasty page has no 1205 inscription; the Chandelas_of_Jejakabhukti title redirects to the same page); Sistan vassalage 1162-1212 added from the Sistan page (the Nasrid dynasty). REPAIR fx-06 (2026-11-01): the 1152 shape (keyframes 1152, 1173, 1175) loses Bactria (131 cells that the Seljuk governor of Balkh held in 1153), and the 1188 and 1192 shapes (keyframes 1188, 1192, 1198, 1200, 1201) lose Yazd, Semnan, Hormozgan, Golestan and Esfahan, which Cliopatria's Ghurid row draws although the Ghurid page is silent on them (page: Ghurid reach at 'the Seljuks of Kerman', Herat 1175, Khorasan 1200). Not changed: Kerman, Sistan and Baluchestan and South Khorasan in the 1188 and 1192 shapes, and Farah (Seljuk shapes 1169-1187 also hold 156 cells of it; the size rule gives it to the Ghurids). REVIEW fx-06 (2026-11-01): the Bactria cut of the 1152 shape holds for 1152-1153 only (Husayn captured at Nab, Seljuk governor of Balkh 1153); from 1154 the new keyframe ghurid-dynasty_1154 and keyframes 1173 and 1175 leave out only Balkh province, because the Ghurid dynasty page has Husayn, after two years as a prisoner, 'conquer Garchistan, Tukharistan, Zamindawar, Bust, Bamiyan and other parts of Khurasan'.
